title: audit
description: The audit trail's write path: the split writer, and the jobs that seal, verify and prune what it writes. Names follow docs/reference/configuration.md.
_comment: Nothing is required here that the template already refuses to render without (see charts/audit/testdata/refusals.txt and templates/_checks.tpl, which fail with a sentence saying why). The schema catches typos and wrong types, and holds every key name to what the templates and values.yaml actually read — it is what caught testdata/values/stream.yaml's workloadIdentity/networkPolicy mis-indentation. Enums are deliberately omitted from fields the templates already validate with a human-readable `fail` message (`mode`, `lockMode`, `keys.provider`, `query.searcher`): a schema enum would refuse those values first, with Helm's own generic message, and testdata/refuse.sh checks for the template's own wording.

consumers.description: How many writer replicas consume the stream, in `mode: stream`. Scales with the record rate.

writer.description: The writers that consume the stream, in `mode: stream`.

replicas.description: How many front-door pods there are (the receiver in `mode: stream`, the single process in `mode: direct`). More than one needs `database` and, with the `local` key provider, a shared directory.

mode.description: How the write path is arranged: `direct` (one process, no stream) or `stream` (a receiver plus `writer.consumers` writers). The chart refuses any other word.

bucket.description: The archive bucket. Required: the writer has nowhere to write without it.

kmsKey.description: A KMS key (ARN or alias) that encrypts the archive at rest, or signs the digest when set under `jobs.digest.kmsKey`.

existingSecret.description: An existing Secret with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (and optionally AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) for a store with no pod identity. Empty keeps the pod's ambient identity.

lockMode.description: The Object Lock mode every object is written in: `compliance`, `governance` or `none`. The chart refuses any other word, and refuses a mode weaker than a composed profile demands.

governance.description: Deprecated: the same as `lockMode: governance`. Set one or the other, never both.

issuers.description: The issuers trusted to name a calling workload.

enabled.description: Rollups at index time and a monthly immutable statement. Needs a profile composed from a metering preset.
A usage consumer, an hourly reconciler and a decision point in front of the application. Needs `mode: stream`.
